promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, please do not run every day yet. Your legs, tendons and feet are still getting used to the pounding, and the gains from a run actually show up on the rest day that follows. Three run days with rest or a dog walk in between is the sweet spot for the next few weeks. Once you can comfortably run the full 5 km in training, we can talk about a fourth short day, but we have time, so let the body bank each session first.

new.analysis:
You did the hardest week of the block: the first one. Three runs, no pain, calves grumbling but recovering, and effort sitting in an easy zone. That is exactly the base I want to build on.

The plan grows total time by about ten minutes and keeps the pattern you already run on. Monday and Wednesday stay around 20 minutes so your body sees the same stress twice, and Saturday stretches to roughly 28 minutes as the one slightly longer effort. Keep your walk-run intervals the same as last week; we will lengthen the run portions in a week or two, not now.

Treat the rest days as training. A dog walk is perfect, nothing brisk, nothing long. If a calf is still tight when you wake up for a run, swap that run for a 20 minute walk and tell me in the next check-in.

The race is ten weeks out, which is plenty of runway for a continuous 5 km. The pattern will be: build time on feet for a few weeks, then slowly swap walk breaks for easy running, then practise the full distance before race day. Nothing fancy, just repeat weeks that look a lot like this one.
